about.title: Placentia Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Placentia's mix of shopping centers, apartment communities, and older sidewalks near Orangethorpe Avenue and the SR-57 corridor means falls happen in parking lots, stairwells, and store aisles more often than people expect. When a property owner in Orange County fails to fix a known hazard or warn visitors about it, California law may allow the injured person to seek compensation. But proving the owner knew, or should have known, about the danger takes work: photos of the hazard, witness names, incident reports, and surveillance footage that businesses often erase within days or weeks. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, that connects you with an independent Placentia-area attorney who can help gather that evidence quickly and explain your options. There's no fee unless the attorney recovers compensation for you, and reaching out costs nothing.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Placentia Fall

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help track down maintenance logs, prior complaints, or repair records that establish this.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Placentia businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days. Quick legal help can mean a formal request to preserve that video before it's gone.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly distracted or hurried, you may still recover a reduced amount based on the other party's share of responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Placentia?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government entity, like the City of Placentia, owns the property, the deadline is much shorter and involves an early claim filing requirement. It's best to get guidance soon after the fall so no deadlines are missed.

items.question: What if I fell in a parking lot near Orangethorpe Avenue or SR-57?
items.answer: Parking lots along busy corridors like Orangethorpe Avenue often have uneven pavement, potholes, or poor lighting. If the property owner or manager knew about the condition and didn't fix it or post a warning, that can support a claim. Documenting the spot with photos right away helps preserve evidence.

items.question: Do I need proof the property owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Yes, California premises liability law generally requires showing the owner had actual or constructive notice of the dangerous condition. This might come from prior complaints, inspection records, or how long the hazard existed before your fall. An attorney can help investigate and gather this proof.
